entries.meaning: The buying and selling of goods, or a skilled job learned by training. ---
examples: Trade between the two countries has doubled since 2019.
He learned a trade instead of going to college.
The new tariffs hurt small shops that live on cross-border trade.
entries.countability: both — countable and uncountable with different meanings

entries.meaning: A branch of business that makes one kind of product, or manufacturing as a whole. ---
examples: She spent twenty years in the music industry.
Heavy industry still employs a lot of people up north.
Several industries were hit hard by the shutdown.
entries.countability: both — countable and uncountable with different meanings

entries.meaning: A large business that the law treats as a single person. ---
examples: The corporation moved its head office to Texas.
Big corporations pay far less tax than most people think.
She left a huge corporation to run a bakery.

entries.meaning: A company, especially one that sells professional services. ---
examples: He works for a law firm downtown.
The firm has offices in six cities.
Two accounting firms bid on the audit.

entries.meaning: A building where goods are made by machine in large numbers. ---
examples: Her father worked at the factory for thirty years.
The factory runs three shifts a day.
Half the factories along the river closed in the nineties.

entries.meaning: A large building where goods are stored before they are sold or shipped. ---
examples: Your order is still sitting in the warehouse in Memphis.
They rented a warehouse out by the airport.
Both warehouses are full through the holidays.

entries.meaning: The right to run a business under a big company's name, or a store run that way. ---
examples: He bought a pizza franchise in Tulsa.
The franchise costs about two hundred thousand up front.
There are over forty franchises in the state.

entries.meaning: A business owned by two or more people, or a working tie between companies. ---
examples: The two of them formed a partnership right out of school.
The partnership fell apart over money.
We have partnerships with three local farms.

entries.meaning: Rivalry between sellers, or an organized contest. ---
examples: There's a lot of competition in the coffee business.
We keep an eye on what the competition is charging.
She won a baking competition at the state fair.
entries.countability: both — countable and uncountable with different meanings

entries.meaning: A senior person who helps run a company and makes the big decisions. ---
examples: The executive who hired me is retiring.
Three executives resigned in the same week.
She's an executive at a software company.

entries.meaning: A company that provides goods or materials to another company. ---
examples: Our main supplier raised prices again.
We switched suppliers after the delays.
The supplier ships out of Ohio.

entries.meaning: A person or company that sells something, especially to a business or on the street. ---
examples: A street vendor was selling hot dogs on the corner.
We pay our vendors within thirty days.
The software vendor handles all the updates.

entries.meaning: A business that sells goods directly to the public. ---
examples: The retailer is closing forty stores.
Online retailers took most of the holiday traffic.
We sell through one big retailer and our own site.

entries.meaning: A company that makes goods in large quantities. ---
examples: The manufacturer covers the parts for two years.
Most of these manufacturers are overseas.
Call the manufacturer before you take it apart.

entries.meaning: Someone who buys something, or whose job is buying stock for a store. ---
examples: The house had three buyers interested in one weekend.
She's a buyer for a department store.
We finally found a buyer for the truck.

entries.meaning: The series of jobs a person holds over a working life.
examples: She spent her whole career in banking.
Teaching is a good career if you can live with the pay.
Both careers took off after they moved west.
entries.contrast: Don't mix up career (kuh-REER) with carrier (KA-ree-ur), a company that hauls freight.
